title: Autoscale signature mismatch and cold-pool strategy review
creator: Liam Nguyen
description:
Summary: During a capacity fluctuation on 2025-02-24 we observed a multi-hour degradation of tail latency for hosted text-generation routes (p95 → p99 increase from ~220ms to >2s) and a sustained drop in throughput for a subset of customers. The root cause was an interaction between our KEDA scaler sampling window, proxy-level request coalescing, and a new kube-probe tuning rollout that changed readiness probe timings. Concretely: (1) KEDA's external/custom scaler observed a burst pattern signature (short spike then quiet) that our percentile-based HPA policy mis-classified as sustained load due to sampling misalignment; (2) HPA reacted by aggressively scaling down under the assumption that the backend could be reprovisioned quickly, but our cold pool/warm-pool prewarming strategy had been partially disabled in the prior deployment, causing cold starts with elevated model load times; (3) the readiness probe timing changes caused transient probe failures that produced false-positive scale-down decisions in the controller. Together this produced a cascade: aggressive scale down → cold starts on subsequent bursts → increased latencies → more retries from clients → perceived sustained load on different signals.

Timeline (high-level):
- 2025-02-24 10:02 UTC: First alert from latency SLI (p99 > 2s) on text-gen-prod-west.
- 10:05-10:20 UTC: Automated scaling occurred downward on 3 node pools; KEDA external scaler returned lower metric values due to short sampling window alignment with proxy coalescing.
- 10:25 UTC: Traffic retry amplification observed; customers reported degraded experience.
- 11:10 UTC: Mitigation - manual hold on autoscaler via emergency override and re-enable warm-pool prewarm flag.
- 12:00 UTC: Latency partially recovered; engineering triage begins.

Technical findings and why this is unique:
- Sampling misalignment: The KEDA scaler was configured with a 30s scrape interval while the proxy's request batching window is 200ms — this caused KEDA to under-sample high-frequency microbursts and then overreact when the next aggregated sample arrived.
- Percentile aggregation mismatch: The HPA policy uses a 95th-percentile CPU signal computed in K8s metrics pipeline. Because bursts were short and high, percentile over the configured window smoothed them into a lower steady value, producing scale-down decisions that didn't reflect the immediate latency risk.
- Readiness probe regressions: A kube-probe tuning change (reduced initialDelaySeconds) rolled earlier in the week meant some pods were marked ready before the runtime completed model KV cache priming, producing transient 503s that the autoscaler interpreted as lowering load or unready pods differently across the cluster.
- Warm-pool gap: The warm-pool feature (pre-started containers with model loaded) had its orchestration lambda disabled by an unrelated change to the deployment job; many nodes were spun down to zero without warm instances available.

Mitigations applied during incident:
- Emergency autoscaler hold (manual override) to prevent further aggressive downsizing.
- Re-enabled warm-pool prewarm flag for affected pools and scaled warm pool to target min=2 per AZ.
- Rolled back the kube-probe initialDelaySeconds change in the affected release channel.
- Short-term increase of HPA minReplicas for high-sensitivity routes to reduce oscillation.

Actionable root causes:
- Operational: deployment job inadvertently disabled warm-pool orchestration (human/config error).
- Design: misconfigured sampling windows between KEDA and upstream proxies; percentile windowing mismatch for bursty LLM workloads.
- Process: no end-to-end test for request-pattern preservation across proxy → scaler → HPA pipeline during rollout.

Action items (see separate list below with owners and due dates). Links to artifacts and evidence are in attachments. The plan below aims to reduce false positives/negatives in scaling decisions, eliminate cold-start cascades, and harden probe and warm-pool orchestration.
action_items: A1: Implement a new 'burst-detection' feature in the autoscaling service that computes both rate-based and percentile-based signals and exposes a fused signal to KEDA (owner: Asha Patel, due: 2025-03-12)

A2: Align KEDA scrape and metric window defaults with proxy batching semantics; change default KEDA scrape interval to 2s for text-gen pools and add override knobs (owner: Diego Mora, due: 2025-03-08)

A3: Reintroduce warm-pool deployment unit tests in CI that assert prewarm lifecycle is not disabled by job changes; add a canary task that validates warm pool min instances post-deploy (owner: Priya Sharma, due: 2025-03-05)

A4: Update HPA policy docs and add a 'burst-safe' policy profile (minReplicas floor, longer cooldown, conservative downscale) and ship as runtime-1.19 opt-in config (owner: Michael Chen, due: 2025-03-19)
A5: Add a short-term automated circuit that prevents scale-to-zero for routes with model cold-start > 500ms observed in last 24h (owner: Asha Patel, due: 2025-03-10)

A6: Create an observable dashboard (grafana) that highlights misaligned signals: proxy-batched-rate vs KEDA-sampled-rate vs node-cpu-percentile with alerting for divergence (owner: Elena Rossi, due: 2025-03-07)
A7: Postmortem review session with SRE, platform, and SDK teams to align on scaling contracts; derive SLA changes if needed (owner: Liam Nguyen, due: 2025-03-14)
A8: Add end-to-end chaos tests in staging that replay bursty traffic patterns including proxy coalescing and assert autoscaler stability (owner: Diego Mora, due: 2025-04-01)
A9: Revisit readiness probe lifecycle for model priming and add an explicit model-ready endpoint that kube-probe checks to avoid marking pods ready prematurely (owner: Priya Sharma, due: 2025-03-12)
A10: Retroactive audit of deployment jobs for the last 6 weeks to find accidental warm-pool toggle changes; report to infra leadership (owner: Security Squad / Infra Eng, due: 2025-03-09)
